title: Pair and Group Discussions
summary: إزاي تشارك في مناقشة مع زميلك أو مجموعة: تقول رأيك، توافق وتعترض بأدب، تسأل غيرك، وتوصلوا لاتفاق.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن إيه؟

text: In a **pair or group discussion** you share ideas with other students. It is not a speech: you **listen**, **respond**, **agree or disagree politely**, **ask others** for their views and, often, **reach an agreement** together.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن الكلام **مع زمايلك** في مجموعة صغيرة (اتنين، أو ٤). هنا مش مهم بس إنك تقول رأيك، المهم كمان إنك **تسمع** وترد على اللي اتقال، **توافق أو تعترض بأدب**، **تسأل** زميلك الساكت عن رأيه، وفي الآخر توصلوا لـ **قرار** مع بعض.

في الكتاب ده موجود في **كل الوحدات** تقريبًا تحت *Discussion in groups of four* أو *Small-Group Discussion*، والأسئلة مكتوب جنبها أفعال زي **Explain / Analyse / Evaluate**. وفيه أنشطة زي **ترتيب الأسباب والوصول لاتفاق** (Unit 4 – Food waste: *Can you reach an agreement?*)، و**اجتماع لجنة تخطيط** (Unit 5 – Eco-Leaders Programme: *Discuss as a group and agree on a final two-day plan*)، و**Global Skills Roundtable** في Unit 8.
الفرق بين الـ Discussion والـ Presentation

blocks.title: القاعدة الذهبية: رد على اللي قبلك
blocks.text: أضعف طالب في المناقشة هو اللي بيقول رأيه كأنه لوحده ومش سامع حد. أقوى طالب بيبدأ كلامه بإنه يربطه باللي اتقال: *As Omar said,… / I agree with Mariam, and I'd add that…* ده بيبين إنك **سامع وفاهم**.
أفعال الأسئلة: Explain / Analyse / Evaluate

text: The book labels discussion questions with thinking verbs. Each verb asks for a different kind of answer.

blocks.text: الكتاب بيكتب جنب كل سؤال مناقشة فعل. الفعل ده بيقولك **نوع** الإجابة المطلوبة:

rows: اشرح إيه اللي بيحصل أو إزاي
How are young people taking action to protect the environment?
حلل: ليه؟ إيه الأسباب؟ إيه العلاقة؟
Why are young people becoming more active in the fight against climate change?
One reason is that… This is connected to…
قيّم: احكم ورأيك بدليل (لأي درجة؟ مفيد ولا لأ؟)
Do you think young people can make a real difference? Why or why not?
I believe that, to some extent,… because…

blocks.text: المهارات اللي محتاجها في المناقشة + جملها

text: Good group speakers use **functions**: they give opinions, agree, disagree politely, add ideas, ask others, check understanding, interrupt politely, keep the group on topic and summarise.

groups.title: تعترض بأدب
items: I'm not sure I agree. I think …
I understand what you mean. However, …
I agree up to a point, but …

groups.title: تتأكد إنك فاهم
items: Could you explain that again, please?

groups.title: تقاطع بأدب
items: Excuse me, may I say something here?

groups.title: ترجّع المجموعة للموضوع
items: Let's get back to the question.
That's interesting, but we need to focus on …

groups.title: تلخّص (للتقديم للفصل)
items: To sum up, our group thinks that …
Most of us agreed that …, but one member felt …

blocks.text: أدوار المجموعة
في المجموعة اللي من ٤، نظموا نفسكم بأدوار. ده بيخلي المناقشة منظمة وكل واحد يتكلم:

rows: يقرأ السؤال ويتأكد إن كل واحد اتكلم
Let's start. What do you think, Ali?
Can I write that down as our first idea?
يقدّم رأي المجموعة للفصل في الآخر

blocks.text: أمثلة من موضوعات الوحدات

items.en: I see your point, Nour, but family support might be more effective than doing activities alone.
items.ar: بقول لزميلتي إني فاهم كلامها وبعدين باعترض بأدب (Unit 1 – stress).

items.en: Building on what Omar said, notifications also damage our concentration when we study.
items.ar: بضيف على كلام زميلي (Unit 2 – screen time).

items.en: What do you think, Youssef? Have you ever trusted a viral post about history?
items.ar: بسأل زميل ساكت عن رأيه (Unit 3 – social media and history).

items.en: I'd rank overbuying first because it happens every week, not only at festivals.
items.ar: بشارك في ترتيب الأسباب (Unit 4 – food waste).

items.en: What if we started the workshop with a beach clean-up and then moved to the debate?
items.ar: باقترح فكرة في اجتماع اللجنة (Unit 5 – Eco-Leaders).

items.en: So, are you saying that fishermen should be part of the decision?
Sorry to interrupt, but I think we're moving away from the question.
So, we all agree that vocational schools need more links with real companies.
items.ar: بلخّص الاتفاق في الآخر (Unit 8 – vocational education).

blocks.text: مناقشة نموذجية (Model Discussion)
دي مناقشة لمجموعة من ٤ على سؤال **Evaluate** من **Unit 5**. اقرأها وشوف كل واحد بيعمل إيه. الأسماء ملهاش علاقة بأي حد حقيقي:

blocks.title: Model group discussion (4 students, about 3 minutes)
blocks.task: Discussion in groups of four. Evaluate: Do you think young people can make a real difference in solving the climate crisis? Why or why not?
text: **Ali (leader):** OK, let's start. The question is whether young people can make a real difference in the climate crisis. Mariam, what do you think?

**Mariam:** I think they can, to a large extent. Young people are very active online, so they can spread awareness quickly. For example, in the text, a girl from Luxor started a Nile clean-up with five friends, and it grew to over two hundred volunteers in a year.
**Omar:** That's a good point, and I'd add that young people are also inventing solutions. The engineering student built a low-cost solar water heater. That's real change, not just talking.

**Nour:** I see your point, Omar, but I'm not sure I agree completely. A clean-up or one heater is great, but the climate crisis is huge. Big changes, like solar parks, need governments and companies.
**Ali:** So, are you saying that young people can't really make a difference, Nour?
**Nour:** Not exactly. I mean they can make a difference, but they can't solve the problem alone.
**Mariam:** I agree with Nour up to a point. However, young people can also push governments to act. When thousands of students speak up, leaders listen.
**Ali:** We have one minute left. Shall we agree on a final answer?
**Omar:** How about this: young people can make a real difference by raising awareness and starting local projects, but they need support from governments to make large-scale change.
**Ali:** Great. So, to sum up, our group thinks young people can make a real difference, especially locally, but the biggest changes need everyone working together.
notes: **Ali (القائد):** بدأ بإعادة السؤال، وسأل زميلة بالاسم، وسأل سؤال توضيح (*So, are you saying…?*)، وانتبه للوقت، ولخّص في الآخر.
**Mariam:** رأي بدرجة (*to a large extent*) + سبب + **دليل من نص الوحدة** = JRE صغيرة جوه المناقشة.
**Omar:** وافق وضاف فكرة جديدة (*That's a good point, and I'd add that…*) بدل ما يكرر نفس الكلام.
**Nour:** اعترضت بأدب (*I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree completely*)، ولما اتسألت وضّحت قصدها (*Not exactly. I mean…*).
**Mariam تاني:** *I agree with Nour up to a point. However,…* = اعتراف + رد.
**الوصول لاتفاق:** *Shall we agree…? / How about this:…* ← ده المطلوب في أنشطة الكتاب (*agree on a final plan / reach an agreement*).
كل دور قصير (جملة لـ ٣ جمل)، وكل واحد **بيرد على اللي قبله**: ده سر المناقشة الناجحة.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء
items: ✗ تقول رأيك وتسكت ومتسمعش حد ← ✓ ابدأ بربط كلامك باللي اتقال: *As Ali said,…*
✗ *You are wrong.* / *No, this is wrong.* ← ✓ *I see your point, but…*
✗ واحد بيتكلم طول الوقت ← ✓ القائد يسأل الساكت: *What do you think, Sara?*
✗ تتكلم عربي مع المجموعة وتترجم في الآخر ← ✓ المناقشة كلها بالإنجليزي حتى لو جملك بسيطة.
✗ تتكلموا كلكم في وقت واحد ← ✓ *Sorry to interrupt, but…* واستنى دورك.
✗ تخلصوا من غير قرار ← ✓ *So, we all agree that…*

blocks.title: لو إنت خجول أو الإنجليزي بتاعك ضعيف
items: احفظ ٣ جمل بس: *I agree with … because…* / *I see your point, but…* / *What do you think?*
اكتب فكرة واحدة ومثال واحد قبل المناقشة.
اتكلم **بدري** في المناقشة: كل ما تستنى أكتر كل ما التوتر يزيد.
سؤال زميلك (*Can you give an example?*) مشاركة كاملة ومحسوبة لك.

blocks.text: إزاي بييجي في الأسئلة؟
الأنشطة في الكتاب بتيجي بالأشكال دي:
**١) أسئلة Explain / Analyse / Evaluate لمجموعة من ٤** ← كل واحد يجاوب سؤال وبعدين الباقي يعلقوا.
**٢) Rank and agree** (Unit 4):

text: Rank the causes of food waste from most serious to least serious: overbuying, poor storage, festivals, misunderstanding labels. Compare your ranking with another group. Can you reach an agreement?

blocks.text: **الحل:** *I'd put overbuying first because it happens every week. — I see your point, but I think misunderstanding labels is more serious because people throw away food that is still safe. — How about putting overbuying first and labels second? — OK, we agree.* ← لاحظ: رأي + سبب + اعتراض مؤدب + اقتراح + اتفاق.

**٣) Planning meeting** (Unit 5): *Each person presents their ideas… Discuss as a group and agree on a final plan… Present your group's programme using claim + reason + evidence.* ← استخدم جمل الكتاب: *I think we should include… / What if we started with…? / I agree / disagree because…*
تدريب
**A) Choose the correct answer from a, b, c or d.**

items.q:
1. You want to disagree politely. You say:
a. That's stupid.
b. I see your point, but I think the opposite is true.
c. No!
d. You don't understand anything.
items.a: **b** — اعتراف إنك سامع + اعتراض مؤدب.

items.q:
2. A group member is quiet. The leader says:
a. Be quiet.
b. Let's finish.
c. What do you think, Hana?
d. I'm the best speaker.
items.a: **c** — بنسأل الساكت عن رأيه.

items.q:
3. You didn't understand your partner. You say:
a. Do you mean that schools should ban phones completely?
b. Whatever.
c. I agree.
d. Next question.
items.a: **a** — سؤال للتأكد (checking understanding).

items.q:
4. The group is talking about football instead of the question. You say:
a. I love football too!
b. Let's get back to the question.
c. Goodbye.
d. Football is boring.
items.a: **b** — بترجع المجموعة للموضوع.

items.q:
5. "Evaluate" in a discussion question means:
a. describe what happened
b. give your judgement with reasons and evidence
c. copy the text
d. count the words
items.a: **b** — Evaluate = احكم وقول رأيك بدليل.

items.q:
6. Which sentence **adds** to a partner's idea?
a. I disagree.
b. Building on what Omar said, recycling also saves energy.
c. Can you repeat?
d. Time is up.
items.a: **b** — Building on what … said = بضيف على كلامه.

blocks.text: **B) Complete the discussion with a suitable phrase.**

items.q:
7. A: I think brands influence teenagers more than parents do.
B: ______, because teenagers see adverts all day on social media.
items.a: **I agree with you** / **That's a good point** — موافقة + سبب.

items.q:
8. A: Sport is the only way to reduce stress.
B: ______, but reading and art can help too.
items.a: **I see your point** / **I agree up to a point** — اعتراض جزئي.

items.q:
9. A: We should start the eco-workshop with a lecture.
B: ______ we started with a practical activity, like planting trees?
items.a: **What if** we started with… — اقتراح (من جمل الكتاب في Unit 5).

items.q:
10. A: Hobbies are a waste of time for students.
B: ______? Can you give an example?
items.a: **Why do you think that?** — بتطلب سبب ودليل.

items.q: 11. Leader: We have one minute left. ______ on a final rule?
items.a: **Shall we agree** on a final rule? — بداية الوصول لاتفاق.

items.q: 12. Reporter: ______, our group thinks that free returns should be limited to faulty items.
items.a: **To sum up** / **We decided that** — تلخيص للفصل.

blocks.text: **C) What would you say in each situation?**

items.q: 13. You want to say something while your partner is still talking.
items.a: *Sorry to interrupt, but can I just add something?*

items.q: 14. Your partner gives an opinion with no evidence.
items.a: *That's interesting. Can you give an example?*

items.q: 15. The group has two different rankings for the causes of food waste.
items.a: *How about putting overbuying first, because we all mentioned it, and then discussing the others?*

items.q: 16. You agree with one part of your partner's idea but not all of it.
items.a: *I agree with you up to a point. It's true that…, but…*

items.q: 17. You are the reporter and the group did not fully agree.
items.a: *Most of us agreed that…, but one member felt that… because…*

blocks.text: **D) Discussion practice: ناقش مع زمايلك في ٣ دقايق.** (أفكار نموذجية تبدأ بيها)

items.q: 18. (Unit 1 – Analyse) How does the writer's purpose affect the language choices they make?
items.a: A writer who wants to **sell** uses emotional words and absolute language. A writer who wants to **inform** uses facts, numbers and neutral, careful language like *may* and *suggests*.

items.q: 19. (Unit 1 – Evaluate) To what extent is it fair to hold individuals responsible for their own poor health choices?
items.a: Only to some extent: people choose what they eat, **but** access to safe parks, money and education also matters. **Example:** gym fees can be too expensive for some families.

items.q: 20. (Unit 2) Which leisure activity is best for teenagers' well-being: sport, creative arts or gaming?
items.a: Sport for the body and stress. Arts for expressing feelings and flexibility of thinking. Gaming only with time limits. **Possible agreement:** a mix is best.

items.q: 21. (Unit 1 – Analyse) Can the same information be presented differently depending on the audience? Give an example.
items.a: Yes: a museum guide for children uses stories and pictures, while a history documentary uses dates and experts. The facts should stay the same, but the language changes.

items.q: 22. (Unit 4) Rank: overbuying, poor storage, festivals, misunderstanding labels. Agree on the most serious.
items.a: Overbuying happens weekly. Labels: people throw away safe food because of the date. **Possible agreement:** overbuying first, labels second, because both happen at home every week.

items.q: 23. (Unit 6) Have you ever seen someone take action to protect an animal, place or cause? What did they do?
items.a: A neighbour feeding street cats and taking them to a vet. A school group cleaning the beach in Alexandria. Explain **what** they did and **why** it mattered.

items.q: 24. (Unit 8) Global Skills Roundtable: choose a vocational field and explain its importance.
items.a: Cybersecurity: students **are learning** to protect networks. It is important because more services **are moving** online. Countries should cooperate because cyberattacks cross borders. (The book asks for two present continuous sentences and one idiom, e.g. *better safe than sorry*.)

items.q: 25. (Unit 9) What can schools do to help new students feel that they belong?
items.a: A buddy system, welcome activities, clubs. **Evidence:** a new student who joins a club makes friends faster. **Possible agreement:** every new student gets a buddy for the first month.

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: المناقشة = **تسمع وترد**: اربط كلامك باللي قبلك (*As … said / Building on …*).
اعترض **بأدب**: *I see your point, but… / I agree up to a point, but…*
اسأل غيرك (*What do you think?*)، واتأكد إنك فاهم (*Do you mean…?*).
اعرف الفعل: **Explain** اشرح، **Analyse** حلل الأسباب، **Evaluate** احكم بدليل.
اقفلوا بـ **اتفاق** وتلخيص: *Shall we agree…? / To sum up, our group thinks…*
